java.say: The domain defines the interface it needs, PaymentProvider. It belongs to the high level.
It gets a provider through its constructor. It does not choose which one.
The Mollie class implements the domain's interface. Now the detail depends on the abstraction: the dependency is turned around.
Only this class knows the Mollie library.
At start-up, one place chooses the provider. Another provider is a new class; CashRegister does not change.
